Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Priya from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to see the console.
[00:11] Dana: Yeah, hi, thanks. We want to focus on cost attribution per route and how to see regressions, cause we're running multiple models and need to tie spend back to product teams.
[00:22] Priya: Awesome, that's exactly what we planned to demo. We'll jump into the Console, show the Usage Analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown views. Note there might be a few captions off, the auto-transcript sometimes munges technical terms.
[00:34] Jordan: Quick agenda - 1) high-level usage trends and SLOs, 2) per-route dashboards and filters (team, model, route), 3) token-level costing and recommendations, 4) Q&A and next steps.
[00:44] Renee: Sounds good. Our main constraints: 200 req/s burst capacity for triage, PII needs to be redacted at the edge, and we have a three-week pilot window.
[00:54] Priya: Got it. I'll start screen share. I'm pulling up the Console now - Home -> Usage analytics. The landing chart is a rolling 7-day active tokens and request counts. You can see trends and, uh, the anomaly detection flags we added. The UI shows per-model and per-route breakdowns in the right pane.
[01:15] [screen share noise] Priya: So here we have a top table - routes are grouped by route name, owner tag, model variant. You can click a route and get the route detail page. For example 'triage-summarize-v2' shows throughput, p50/p95 latency, and token consumption per call.
[01:33] Samir: Is that token consumption inclusive of system prompt + user prompt + response?
[01:37] Priya: Yes, total tokens. We also have a token split UI - you can toggle to see input vs output tokens and cost per token by model. The cost model uses your selected pricing tier; Jordan will share pricing details after.
[01:50] Dana: Can we map cost back to our product teams? We have internal tagging in headers.
[01:55] Priya: Absolutely - routes support arbitrary metadata tags, and you can group or filter by 'team' tag. The per-route dashboard has an attribution view - daily cost by tag, and a heatmap for spikes.
[02:07] Jordan: One thing customers like is exported CSVs and per-route cost reports that you can ingest into your internal chargeback systems. We also push data into S3 or BigQuery on dedicated plans.
[02:20] Renee: For Private / on-prem, do we still get the console or is it self-hosted?
[02:25] Priya: The control plane can be customer-managed for Private deployments; the Console is available with role-based access. You keep audit logs and the metrics stream - we integrate with your KMS and SIEM. There's a note in our docs: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf and the private deployment guide.
[02:42] Samir: Security is big for us. Are audit logs immutable?
[02:45] Priya: Yes, we write an append-only audit stream; we also support long-term retention as an add-on. For encryption we use KMS/HSM integrations. Sometimes the transcript shows "K V cash" instead of "KV cache" - but yes, caching is supported for prefixes and will show in the cost-savings recommendations.
[03:03] Dana: Can you show the per-route cost breakdown? That's the main thing I need to show my VP.
[03:07] Priya: Jumping to the route detail - here's the cost tab. It shows total spend for the range, cost per call, cost per 1k tokens, and a model-split pie chart. The key is you can compare identical routes across model variants - e.g., for the same prompt the 'gpt-like-128k-q4' variant has 30% lower cost but 20ms higher p95. That tradeoff table is generated by Redwood Optimize heuristics.
[03:33] Samir: Is latency consistent across regions? We have users in US-West and EU.
[03:37] Priya: The Dashboard includes region breakdowns; you can layer region as a secondary dimension. We also surface routing policy impacts - like if you prefer lower-cost variant but same latency SLO we show you the expected tail latency and cost delta.
[03:52] Renee: How does the console compute 'expected tail latency'?
[03:55] Priya: It's based on historical p95/p99 by model and sequence-length buckets, plus an adjustment for autoscaling policy. There's a small model - not a full ML model - it's heuristics derived from our runtime telemetry.
[04:06] Dana: Do you support cohort analysis? We need to see behavior for new users vs power users.
[04:10] Priya: Yes, cohorting is under the 'Advanced filters' - you can create cohorts on any tag or property, and then compare token-per-session, average response length, and per-cohort cost.
[04:20] Jordan: Quick interjection - competitors sometimes show aggregate token counts but not route-level economics. Our differentiator is route-level and owner-level attribution so engineering leads can see exactly where spend is happening.
[04:34] Dana: That helps. Another ask - can the console surface recommendations? For example suggest batching for high QPS low-latency endpoints?
[04:42] Priya: Yes, that's part of Redwood Optimize suggestions. On a route page you'll see suggested batching windows, recommended quantization profiles, and whether prefix caching would yield savings. We surface estimated monthly savings and confidence bands.
[04:56] Samir: Can you show an example recommendation?
[04:58] Priya: Here - triage-summarize-v2 shows 'Enable batching: 5-20ms window' expected to reduce token cost by ~12% at current traffic. Also 'consider q4_0 for non-PII sanitized traffic' with an expected 18% cost drop but a slight increase in variance.
[05:15] Dana: We need to be careful with quantization on clinical text - accuracy matters. Can Redwood run an eval for our metric?
[05:21] Priya: Yes, we can run quality regressions per prompt set. For pilots we run a paired eval and show perplexity/rogue metrics plus a human sampling. We'll include eval hooks in the pilot plan.
[05:33] Renee: For the pilot, how do we do the routing? If Dedicated is down we need fallback to hosted - is that automatic?
[05:39] Jordan: We support smart routing and automatic fallback policies - canary, a/b, and fallback to hosted variants. You configure per-route policies; we recommend a read-only test first.
[05:48] Samir: Pricing - high level?
[05:50] Jordan: I'll send the detailed tiered pricing but high level: hosted per-token with tier discounts; Dedicated has a commit and then lower unit cost and predictable throughput; Private is licensed. I'll share a spreadsheet.
[06:00] Dana: Can you push the per-route CSVs programmatically?
[06:03] Priya: Yes, via the Console export API or scheduled reports to S3/BigQuery.
[06:09] Samir: We have a follow-up question about data retention windows and purge.
[06:13] Priya: Retention is configurable - default 30 days on hosted, longer on Dedicated. We support purge APIs and on Private you control retention.
[06:21] [brief crosstalk] Samir: Great. A bit of nitpick - timestamps in the transcript sometimes skip, I think that's the auto system.
[06:27] Jordan: Totally - auto-transcript not perfect.
[06:30] Priya: Last part - demoing an exported cost report. (narration) I click export, pick range 12/01-12/30, group by team, and the CSV shows day, route, model, tokens, cost, owner tag. You can ingest that in your internal BI.
[06:49] Dana: That export will include our internal route tags, right?
[06:52] Priya: Yes, route metadata is preserved, we don't alter your tags.
[06:56] Renee: Any guardrails for PII leaking into logs?
[06:59] Priya: We have configurable redaction at the edge and on ingestion. Also support for tokenization-based scrubbing; but that needs to be set up in your pipeline. We'll include our security docs.
[07:11] Samir: Ok good. Let's recap next steps.
[07:14] Jordan: Recap - Jordan to send pricing + Dedicated/Private options and the export template; Priya to schedule a 24-hour benchmark with the sample prompts; Dana to share prompt set and traffic profile; schedule follow-up pilot review. Links I'm dropping in chat: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/console-usage.pdf ; Security: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf ; Export API docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/export-api
[07:36] Dana: One more, can you include a quick runbook for troubleshooting latency spikes?
[07:40] Priya: Yes, we'll attach a short runbook and a checklist for tuning batch windows and autoscaling.
[07:46] Samir: Thanks all.
[07:48] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up early next week.
